items.definition: a persistent feeling of inadequacy and self-doubt, typically manifesting as anxiety or defensiveness about one's worth or abilities compared to others
items.example: His inferiority complex stemmed from years of parental criticism, causing him to avoid situations where he might be evaluated.

items.definition: information, understanding, or skill acquired through experience or education; the state of being aware of or familiar with something
items.example: Her knowledge of Renaissance art made her an invaluable consultant on the museum's restoration project.

items.definition: to be inclined or prone to do something habitually or characteristically; to show a general pattern or direction
items.example: Young professionals tend to prioritize career advancement over work-life balance in their first few years.
items.verbSentence: Studies have shown that adolescents ___ to process risk differently than adults.

items.definition: a response indicating that the answer to a question cannot be determined without knowing further circumstances or conditions; used to express that the outcome is contingent on additional factors
items.example: When asked whether remote work improves productivity, most managers say it depends on the type of role and individual worker.

items.definition: a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit with a deep orange colour and a sweet, mildly acidic flavour; also, the colour itself
items.example: The tangerine trees in the orchard bore an abundant crop that year, their branches heavy with ripe fruit.

items.definition: to attempt to find or obtain something; to pursue a particular goal, outcome, or person deliberately
items.example: The company is actively seeking qualified candidates with experience in artificial intelligence and machine learning.
items.verbSentence: After the scandal, she decided to ___ legal advice before making any public statement.

items.definition: to happen or occur in a particular way; to prove to be the case when discovered or revealed
items.example: The meeting turned out to be far more productive than anyone had anticipated.

items.definition: a small error made in typing or writing, typically involving the omission or misplacement of a letter or word
items.example: The contract contained a single typo that nearly invalidated the entire agreement.

items.definition: to acquire a general sense or preliminary understanding of something; to gain insight into its essential character or style without necessarily mastering it fully
items.example: After attending a few rehearsals, the new member began to get the flavor of it and understood the ensemble's artistic vision.

items.definition: the practice of following and observing someone closely as they carry out their work or activities, typically as a form of learning or training; also, the technique of imitating a speaker in real time while listening to recorded speech, used especially in language learning
items.example: During her internship, she spent two weeks shadowing the senior consultant to understand how client relationships are managed.
items.wordFormationSentence: The intern was asked to ___ the project manager for the entire week.
